subject.title: [Bug]: Runtime tool surface returns blank body after gateway-touching operations; container restart only briefly clears it

question: Which owner path should maintainers treat as canonical for this wedge: deferred gateway restart/session-admission cleanup, tool-result surfacing, or a recovery/status UX gap?
rationale: The current repro evidence is strong enough to keep open, but the failure crosses multiple lifecycle surfaces and the item is already marked no-new-fix-pr, so automation should not choose the fix boundary without maintainer triage.

options.title: Trace live wedged sessions first
options.body: Use the offered session logs/journalctl to identify the exact active-work, restart, compaction, or tool-result state that remains stuck before approving a fix PR.

options.title: Queue a recovery/status UX change
options.body: Add or expose session reset/tool-health recovery only if maintainers decide the product needs an operator-facing escape hatch beyond fixing the underlying wedge.

options.title: Treat it as the primitive-output bug
options.body: Close against the merged primitive-output fix only if logs prove the broader gateway/restart/session symptoms collapse to that already-merged extraction path.

recommendation.title: Trace live wedged sessions first
recommendation.body: Use the offered session logs/journalctl to identify the exact active-work, restart, compaction, or tool-result state that remains stuck before approving a fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The best available routing signal is recent adjacent session-lock and tool-result work, plus broad involvement in current runtime fixes.
